key_insight: A level-set optimization method reshapes Stokes–Darcy interfaces and permits topology changes while enforcing Beavers–Joseph–Saffman coupling.
engineering_relevance: The method supports free-flow/porous-medium interface design to reduce viscous energy dissipation and infer interfaces from velocity measurements.
method: Represent the coupled flow domains and interface with a level-set function.
Derive adjoint sensitivities with a continuously Fréchet-differentiable control-to-state map.
Combine reaction–diffusion level-set evolution with mixed finite elements.
evidence_signal: Two- and three-dimensional numerical experiments verify sensitivities and demonstrate energy minimization and interface reconstruction from partial, noisy velocity observations.
watch_item: The abstract reports numerical validation but does not quantify computational cost or reconstruction accuracy across noise levels.
paper_title: A level-set method for shape and topology optimization of Stokes--Darcy flows with Beavers--Joseph--Saffman coupling
